text:
arjun: heads-up — ran into a confusing failure while demoing the sampleapp. The embed batching helper sent what it thought were 768-dim vectors, but the reranker returned a dim_mismatch.

hema: can you paste the exact request/response (sanitized)? curious if it's a padding vs model-alias issue. :mag_right:

arjun: sanitized request body: {requests:[{id:"r1",embedding:[0.001,0.002,.../*768 floats*/]}], model:"embed-medium-quantized"}
server response: 400 {error:"dim_mismatch", got:256, expected:768, message:"received vector length 256, expected 768"}

taylor: oh interesting — that model alias has a quantized 256 fallback in our catalog (embed-medium-quantized -> embed-medium-256) for low-memory nodes. Looks like the batch helper sometimes substitutes the quantized variant at runtime for speed. That substitution should be explicit.

arjun: right — the helper did an internal model-swap to a fast variant when GPU slot was busy. It logged the new model alias but the sampleapp's retry logic stripped logs, so the request body still claimed embed-medium-quantized. Confusing UX.

hema: another parity note: Go SDK will convert vectors to float32 little-endian byte arrays and leave length untouched; JS SDK will downcast to float16 and collapse dims for quantized variants. That explains 768->256 in some clients. We need a single documented rule.

taylor: propose changes: (1) batch helper MUST include a header X-Client-Embed-Dim with the declared vector length, (2) if the serving runtime chooses a variant with different dim, it must return a clear header X-Server-Embed-Dim and a human-readable error explaining the mismatch, (3) SDKs should surface a DimensionMismatch exception with expected/got fields.

arjun: agree. Also: the retrier doubled the batch once when the first request timed out. There was no Idempotency-Key on the batch request, so reranker accepted both and duplicated scores in the local cache. For scoring pipelines we must dedupe.

hema: let's add Idempotency-Key by default for batch endpoints and require per-item ids in the batch payload. Server should dedupe identical ids within the same key window. This will protect against blind retries.

taylor: small UX addition: when the client sees a dim mismatch returned, the SDK should suggest remediation: (a) pick a compatible model alias from the server's candidates list, (b) set pad_mode=(pad|trim|fail) in client config, or (c) re-run with X-Client-Embed-Dim header if using intentionally quantized vectors.

arjun: wrote a quick example for troubleshooting in the sampleapp README (sanitized):

```
# curl example when your model produces 256-dim vectors but reranker expects 768
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/re-rank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Client-Embed-Dim: 256" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-medium-quantized","requests":[{"id":"r1","embedding":[...]}]}'
```

hema: perfect. Also add CI lint that fails when sampleapp fixtures have vectors that don't match the configured sampleapp.embedding_dim. That will catch these drifts earlier.

taylor: for SDK parity: surface model.metadata.embedding_dim in all SDKs at model load time and emit a startup warning if sampleapp.config.embedding_dim != model.metadata.embedding_dim. Also standardize response field names to `embedding` / `embeddings`.

arjun: i've opened a small PR in sampleapp with: dim validator in the batch helper, Idempotency-Key injection, and a compatibility shim mapping `vector`->`embedding`. Links in PR description show logs and failing test.

devx-bot: Created DEVEX-4001: "embed: batch dim header + idempotency + server candidate list" and linked this thread.

ops-bot: FYI staged deploy will include server-side header X-Server-Embed-Dim and a new machine-readable error shape: {"error":"dim_mismatch","got":256,"expected":768,"candidates":["embed-medium-768","embed-large-768"]}.

hema: nice. once server lands i'll flip on the stricter client validator in the sampleapp CI. For now keep pad_mode opt-in.

taylor: one more thought — add metrics: embed_dim_mismatch_count{client_dim,server_dim,model_alias} and a tracing span when pad_mode changes vectors. SRE asked for that.

arjun: thanks all — this should make onboarding less painful. i'll add a short troubleshooting card to the devex docs linking the curl example and the common causes (quantized fallback, silent pad in JS, retry duplication).

hema: i'll coordinate SDK patches (python/js/go) to expose metadata and add DimensionMismatch exception mapping. rough ETA: next week.

taylor: i'll review the sampleapp PR and the CI lint. thanks! :thumbsup:

arjun: resolved for now — closing this demo follow-up. :white_check_mark:
